title: Vacation

constraints.text: N ≤ 1e5, three activities per day, no activity two days in a row

explanation: Add yesterday's activity to the state: dp over days with 3 columns, one per activity.
traps: Picking the best activity each day greedily breaks the 'no repeat' rule in later days.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[i][a] = max happiness over days 1..i if day i's activity is a

options.why: Loses which activity was done on day i, so you can't forbid repeating it.

options.text: dp[i][mask] = max happiness where mask is the set of activities used so far
options.why: The rule is about consecutive days, not about which activities were ever used.

options.text: dp[a][b][c] = max happiness having done each activity a, b, c times
options.why: Counts don't matter; only yesterday's choice does.

extraLayers.explanation: The constraint only looks one day back, so remembering the last activity (3 options) is enough.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: dp[i][a] = gain(i, a) + max over b ≠ a of dp[i−1][b]
dp[i][a] = gain(i, a) + max over all b of dp[i−1][b]
options.why: Allows b = a, i.e. the same activity two days in a row.
Never adds the gains up across days.
That forces the same activity every day, which is exactly what's forbidden.

extraLayers.explanation: Today's best with activity a = today's gain + yesterday's best with any different activity.
